recent_posts.title: Crystal 1.20.1 is released!
recent_posts.summary: Crystal 1.20.1 is a patch release fixing two regressions from 1.20.0. Kernel TLS support, introduced in 1.20.0, had production issues — some were fixed but it has been disabled by default, with an opt-in flag available via OpenSSL::SSL::Options::ENABLE_KTLS. A regression in Range#sample that could cause loss of randomness was also fixed. The release includes 9 changes from 2 contributors.

recent_posts.title: Crystal 1.19.2 is released!
recent_posts.summary: Crystal 1.19.2 is a patch release fixing two regressions and a security vulnerability. The security fix addresses HTTP request smuggling (CWE-444): HTTP::Server previously accepted requests with both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding headers, prioritizing Content-Length, which could allow smuggling attacks when behind a vulnerable frontend. The fix rejects such requests and ignores Content-Length when Transfer-Encoding is present. Additionally, a regression in Range#sample that could lose randomness is fixed. The release includes 3 changes from 2 contributors.

recent_posts.title: Crystal 1.20.0 is released!
recent_posts.summary: Crystal 1.20.0 is out with 161 changes from 21 contributors. Key highlights include a new @[TargetFeature] annotation for per-function CPU feature targeting (enabling portable SIMD with AVX2/AVX512 alternatives), a preview of a new ergonomic Process API treating command lines as string arrays with Process.capture and Process.capture_result, a preview io_uring event loop for Linux, and Kernel TLS support on Linux and FreeBSD. The release also adds M:N scheduling improvements to execution contexts (planned for default in 1.21), a security fix for HTTP request smuggling via conflicting Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding headers, compiler defaults to mold or lld linkers when available, and various stdlib improvements to StringScanner, HTTP::WebSocket sub-protocol negotiation, and OptionParser option bundling.

recent_posts.title: Official Linux ARM64 builds
recent_posts.summary: Crystal 1.19 introduces official Linux ARM64 builds, ending a long wait for ARM64 support on Linux. The builds are available across all existing distribution channels including nightly builds, release tarballs, Docker images, Snap packages, and the install-crystal GitHub Action. Previously, Crystal supported ARM64 as a tier 1 architecture only for macOS; now Linux users on ARM64 hardware have full official support.

recent_posts.title: Crystal talk at FOSDEM 2026
recent_posts.summary: Johannes Müller is presenting an introductory talk about the Crystal programming language at FOSDEM 2026 in Brussels on Sunday, February 1st at 09:00. The talk, titled "Crystal: A language for humans and computers," will cover core concepts of Crystal in the Declarative and Minimalistic Computing track. The presentation will be recorded, and there's potential for an informal Crystal meetup during the conference.

recent_posts.title: Crystal 1.19.1 is released!
recent_posts.summary: Crystal 1.19.1 has been released as a patch update fixing two regressions introduced in version 1.19.0. The fixes address timer conversion issues that caused sleep() functions to trigger immediately instead of waiting on Darwin, BSD, and Windows platforms. Pre-built packages are available on GitHub Releases and official distribution channels.

recent_posts.title: Crystal 1.19.0 is released!
recent_posts.summary: Crystal 1.19.0 introduces execution contexts as a preview feature (enabled with compiler flags), moving toward default multi-threading support in version 1.20. The release adds Time::Instant for monotonic timeline operations, refactors process spawning to use posix_spawn, and includes new synchronization primitives (Sync::Mutex, Sync::RWLock, Sync::ConditionVariable). Standard library additions include methods for NamedTuple, Set, Hash, and Random, plus ARM64 Linux binaries are now available. The compiler now always builds with execution contexts and uses multithreaded LLVM codegen across all platforms including Windows.

recent_posts.title: Crystal 1.18.2 is released!
recent_posts.summary: Crystal 1.18.2 has been released as a patch update fixing two regressions introduced in version 1.18.0. The release addresses a type restriction issue in IO#read_bytes and a bug in Fiber::ExecutionContext.default_workers_count. The update includes 3 changes from 3 contributors, with pre-built packages available on GitHub Releases and official distribution channels.

recent_posts.title: Crystal 1.18.1 is released!
recent_posts.summary: Crystal 1.18.1 has been released as a patch update addressing two regressions from version 1.18.0. The release fixes an issue with enum definition parsing and overly strict type restrictions in HTTP::WebSocket. Pre-built packages are available on GitHub Releases and official distribution channels.

recent_posts.title: Crystal 1.18.0 is released!
recent_posts.summary: Crystal 1.18.0 introduces execution contexts as a preview feature with improved parallel processing capabilities, starting with a single thread that can scale dynamically. The release adds deprecation warnings for types, aliases, and method parameters, updates Time formatting to align with RFC 9557, and enhances serialization with YAML alias resolution and improved JSON/YAML inspection. Standard library additions include new methods for Set, File, SemanticVersion, and Socket operations, while networking improvements fix StaticFileHandler behavior and HTTP client callback handling. The compiler gains better type inference for instance variables and includes performance optimizations for schedulers and event loops.
